a row means. Do NOT copy it back here; issue 1095 is what that cost.

c:client_get_options.why: reads back the options a client was created with. `nros_client_options_t` ships and `nros_client_init_with_options` takes it; what is missing is the READBACK -- no `*_get_options` exists anywhere in our C surface, for any entity. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417): this row said there is no runtime options struct. Seven ship and the correlator buckets all fourteen items `same` -- `nros_{node,publisher,subscription,service,client,action_client,action_server}_options_t` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/nros_generated.h:1461,1729,2011,2474,2537,2556,2592`) plus a `*_get_default_options` for each, and `nros_node_options_t::domain_id_override` is a RUNTIME per-node domain. What is genuinely absent is the LIFECYCLE around one: no `*_options_copy`, no `*_options_fini`, and no `*_get_options` readback anywhere in the C surface.

c:client_get_rmw_handle.why: our RMW seam is the vtable (RFC-0035), not an entity accessor. See `c:node_get_rmw_handle`.

c:client_impl_t.why: rcl's pimpl; our handles carry their state inline. See `c:publisher_impl_t`.

c:client_init.why: phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) -- `rcl_client_init(client, node, type_support, service_name, options)`. No symbol answers to this key; the rclc spelling `rclc_client_init_default` does (`c:client_init_default`, `packages/api/nros-c/src/service.rs:1164`), and the options-shaped forms are `nros_client_init_with_qos` / `_with_options` / `_polling` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/nros_generated.h:6448`, `:6470`, `:6519`). Same reasoning as `c:service_init`, one entity over.

c:client_init_default.why:
rclc's default-QoS wrapper; `nros_client_init` IS the default form. See `c:publisher_init_default`.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) — refuse-loud -> adopt-bounded. `rclc_client_init_default` EXISTS at rclc's arity (`packages/api/nros-c/src/service.rs:1164`) and correlates `same`. The compiler points at argument 3 exactly as for `c:service_init_default`: `const struct nros_service_type_t*` where rclc takes `const rosidl_service_type_support_t*`, an incompatible-pointer diagnostic at the call. The response callback is supplied at registration (`nros_executor_add_client*`), as rclc's is at `rclc_executor_add_client`. See `c:service_init_default` for the envelope.

c:client_init_polling.why: RFC-0022's polling tier. See the pubsub stage's `cpp:PollingSubscription`.

c:client_request_publisher_get_actual_qo.why: see `c:service_request_subscription_get_actual_qos` — the client side of the same pair. LANDED phase-444 (issue 1437) — `nros_client_request_publisher_get_actual_qos`.

c:client_response_subscription_get_actua.why: see `c:service_request_subscription_get_actual_qos` — the client side of the same pair. LANDED phase-444 (issue 1437) — `nros_client_response_subscription_get_actual_qos`.

c:client_send_request_raw.why: the raw form; see the pubsub stage's `c:publish_raw`.

rename.resolution:
Target and shape settled 2026-09-03 by phase-379 W6 decision 2, which amended RFC-0036: "C keeps rcl's literal shape, `nros_ret_t f(args…, T *out)`". One C symbol, `nros_ret_t nros_client_service_is_ready(client, bool *out)`, with the tri-state `-1` arm becoming `NROS_RET_UNSUPPORTED`. C++ and Rust landed in 3941b569a; C is the open residue of issue 1008.

IT IS A SWAP, NOT A RENAME, and nobody had written that down: the target name is ALREADY TAKEN by a differently-shaped function — `bool nros_client_service_is_ready(const client)` (`nros_generated.h:6176`) — while the tri-state lives at `nros_client_server_available(client, int32_t *out)` (`:6141`). So `server_available` loses its name, the bare-bool loses its shape, and the deprecated forwarder must be written for the spelling that is KEEPING its name. Same collision class as `make_publisher`->`create_publisher` (issue 0818), one entity over.

c:client_service_is_ready.why: the correctly-named half of `c:client_server_available`, present only in C. Keeping both is the defect; see that row.

c:client_set_response_callback.why: the reply arrives at a callback bound to the CLIENT at creation, rather than resolving a future. `executor-owns-no-entity-storage` and RFC-0041, on the client side.

c:client_set_timeout.why: a per-client default deadline for a pending request, so a device that must not wait forever states the bound once rather than at every call. rclcpp has no client-level timeout -- the caller passes one to `spin_until_future_complete` each time.

c:client_take_response.why: the ours-only half of `c:take_response`: poll for the reply to the most recent `nros_client_send_request_async`. Renamed from `nros_client_try_recv_response` by phase-379 W6 decision 1 (2026-09-03).

c:client_take_response_raw.why: the L1 polling-client half of `c:take_response`. `reply` -> `response` moved with the verb. Renamed from `nros_client_try_recv_reply_raw` by phase-379 W6 decision 1 (2026-09-03).

c:client_try_recv_reply_raw.why: DEPRECATED SPELLING as of phase-379 W6 decision 1 (2026-09-03); the live name is `nros_client_take_response_raw` and the forwarder is a NROS_DEPRECATED_MSG `static inline` in the hand-written module header, so it adds no exported symbol and no ABI cost. Still on the surface, so still a row. Retired in W7 step 4, in one batch with the rest of the deprecated set. See `c:take`.

c:client_try_recv_response.why: DEPRECATED SPELLING as of phase-379 W6 decision 1 (2026-09-03); the live name is `nros_client_take_response` and the forwarder is a NROS_DEPRECATED_MSG `static inline` in the hand-written module header, so it adds no exported symbol and no ABI cost. Still on the surface, so still a row. Retired in W7 step 4, in one batch with the rest of the deprecated set. See `c:take`.

c:client_wait_for_service.why: blocks until the server appears or the deadline passes, driving the executor. rclcpp's `Client::wait_for_service` folds onto ours by the *Base rule; C's rclc has no counterpart.

c:executor_add_service_raw.why:
phase-417 stage 6 — the callback moved OFF `*_init` and onto registration, so `rclc_{subscription,service}_init_default` now matches rclc's four-argument shape and the callback arrives here, exactly as rclc supplies it at `rclc_executor_add_subscription`.

It keeps the `nros_` prefix DELIBERATELY, and that is the whole content of this row. rclc's same-named calls deliver a DESERIALISED message into caller-owned storage; these deliver CDR BYTES. Taking rclc's spelling for a byte-oriented entry point would be a name whose contract differs -- the `PollingSubscription::take()` failure, which had rclcpp's name, rclcpp's signature and the opposite contract, and cost a spinning loop with no compile error.

The faithful rclc-shaped entry point exists beside it and DOES take the name: `nros_executor_add_subscription_typed` (W5.a), reached per-message as `<Msg>_executor_add_subscription(exec, sub, &msg, cb, ctx, invocation)` -- rclc's six arguments in rclc's order. So the two shapes are distinguished by NAME rather than by a reader noticing which one deserialises, which is what RFC-0089 asks for.

c:executor_register_lifecycle_services.why: the same for the five lifecycle services; see `c:executor_register_parameter_services`.

c:executor_register_parameter_services.why: registers the six `rcl_interfaces/srv/*` servers on the executor as one call. rclcpp starts them from `NodeOptions::start_parameter_services` at node construction; ours is explicit because the six queryables are a measurable cost against `ZPICO_MAX_QUERYABLES` (issue 0460) and an image that does not need them should not pay.

c:get_zero_initialized_client.why:
rcl's free-function spelling; see `c:get_zero_initialized_publisher`.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) — refuse-loud -> adopt, a VERDICT BUG. `rcl_get_zero_initialized_client` is exported under rcl's own name (`packages/api/nros-c/src/service.rs:1142`), returns a default `nros_client_t`, and the correlator files it `same`. Nothing refuses; the row promised a diagnostic no compiler emits. RFC-0089's own rule for a `declined` row that correlates `same` is `adopt` — the decline was the error.

c:get_zero_initialized_service.why:
see `c:get_zero_initialized_client`.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) — refuse-loud -> adopt, a VERDICT BUG. `rcl_get_zero_initialized_service` is exported under rcl's own name (`packages/api/nros-c/src/service.rs:220`), returns a default `nros_service_t`, and the correlator files it `same`. Nothing refuses. See `c:get_zero_initialized_client`.

c:qos_services_best_effort.why: phase-417 W5.d. The QoS rclc's `rclc_service_init_best_effort` and `rclc_client_init_best_effort` build INLINE: both copy `rmw_qos_profile_services_default` and flip `reliability` to BEST_EFFORT (`rclc/src/rclc/{service,client}.c` @ `10eadcc`). ROS 2 gives that value no name -- there is no `rmw_qos_profile_services_best_effort` -- so the two nano-ros presets that need it would otherwise each restate it, which is issue 0160's hand-mirror class at header scale. A `static inline` returning by value in <nros/service.h>: no exported symbol, no writable data, and a caller needs a mutable copy to take the address of. Ours-only because the NAME is ours; the VALUE is upstream's, and `qos::tests::the_rclc_best_effort_presets_choose_between_two_different_profiles` pins the premise a reader gets wrong -- the depth stays 10 here, where the pub/sub `_best_effort` presets drop to the sensor profile's 5.

c:response_callback_t.why: RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-18 (phase-417 W5.e follow-through), divergence -> extension, on the client side of `c:service_callback_t` -- and it is a `see` again only because the argument really is the same one, not because nobody looked. Ours is `void (*)(const uint8_t *response, size_t response_len, void *context)`; rclc's `rclc_client_callback_t` is `void (*)(const void *response)` over a deserialized reply. The typed counterpart ships from the same pack: `<Srv>_response_fn_t = void (*)(const <Srv>_response *, void *context)`, installed with `<Srv>_client_set_response_callback(client, &handler)`, whose trampoline decodes into the caller's `<Srv>_client_handler_t`. A reply whose CDR does not decode does NOT reach the callback: handing it a zeroed struct would be indistinguishable from a server that answered with defaults.

c:send_request.why:
CORRECTED 2026-08-26 (phase-379 W5), re-verdicted rename -> divergence, with two factual errors fixed.
(1) There is no bare `nros_client_send_request` -- the brace spelling `nros_client_send_request{,_async,_raw}` claimed one. Verified word-boundary, repo-wide: the C API ships exactly `nros_client_send_request_async(client, request_data, request_len)` (executor-registered client) and `nros_client_send_request_raw(client, data, len)` (L1 polling-mode client). The `_async` / `_raw` split is two client MODES, not two spellings of one call.
(2) 'only the free-function shape differs' is wrong the same way `c:publish` was: both of ours ARE free functions taking the client first, exactly rcl's shape. `nros_client_` is a module prefix -- rcl uses the identical construction for `rcl_client_fini` / `rcl_client_request_publisher_get_actual_qos`. And the chain of precedent argues the other way in any case: `c:get_zero_initialized_client` defers to `c:get_zero_initialized_publisher`, which is verdict DECLINED, i.e. it argues for KEEPING our spelling.
What actually differs, and the constraint for each: `rcl_send_request(client, ros_request, sequence_number)` takes a typed `const void *` plus an OUT sequence number. Ours take bytes (`const uint8_t *`, `size_t`) because there is no runtime typesupport dispatch and no allocator to serialize into -- the same reason `c:publish` splits. And neither returns a sequence number because a nano-ros client keeps ONE call in flight (the `in_flight` flag and `reset_in_flight()` on the handle, `nros-node/src/executor/handles.rs`) rather than a correlation table; the backend does hand one back since issue 0778 and the raw handle drops it explicitly rather than by omission. Correlating replies across a client restart is the `rust:RequestId` divergence, one layer down.

rename.resolution: Not a rename. The word `send_request` already matches and so does the free-function shape; the row's remaining argument rested on a symbol spelling that does not exist and on a precedent that is itself `declined`. Re-verdicted to divergence naming the real differences (bytes not `const void *`; no out sequence number, one call in flight). No code change; no target name invented.

c:send_response.why:
RETRACTED as a rename 2026-09-04; re-verdicted `divergence`. Not an `extension` either — `rcl_send_response(service, rmw_request_id_t*, void*)` exists (`rclc.json`, `rcl/service.h`).

The row said ours is "method-style". It is not: `nros_service_send_response_raw(service, sequence_number, data, len)` (`nros_generated.h:5917`) is a FREE FUNCTION taking the service first — rcl's own shape — and `nros_service_` is a module prefix of the construction rcl itself uses (`rcl_client_fini`). This is verbatim the correction already applied to `c:publish` and `c:send_request` on 2026-08-26, and to the receive-side twins `c:take_request`/`c:take_response` on 2026-09-03. This row is the reply-side member of that family and was not swept with it.

What actually differs: `rmw_request_id_t*` (16-byte writer GUID plus sequence) versus a bare `int64_t` — the divergence written up at `rust:RequestId` — and a typed `void*` versus `const uint8_t*` plus `size_t`, because there is no runtime typesupport dispatch and no allocator. The `_raw` suffix belongs to the separate open SERIALIZED-vs-RAW question that `c:publish` owns, not to this row.

rename.resolution: Retracted 2026-09-04 as the fourth member of the c:publish / c:send_request / c:take_* family, all corrected earlier.

c:service_callback_t.why:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-18 (phase-417 W5.e follow-through), divergence -> extension. Both halves of the old one-line reason were false, and they are recorded here rather than smoothed away.

It said: "bound to the entity at creation; see the pubsub stage's `c:subscription_callback_t`."

(1) THE BINDING SITE MOVED. phase-417 stage 6 took the callback off `*_init` and put it at registration -- `nros_executor_add_service_raw(exec, svc, cb, ctx)`, which is where rclc supplies it (`rclc_executor_add_service`). The sentence described an arrangement the tree no longer has. (2) THE ROW IT DEFERRED TO NO LONGER SAYS THAT EITHER: `c:subscription_callback_t` was itself re-verdicted divergence -> extension on 2026-09-13, so a `see` pointing at it was inheriting a retracted argument.

WHAT THE DIFFERENCE ACTUALLY IS: the DATA contract, plus a return. Ours is `bool (*)(const uint8_t *request, size_t request_len, uint8_t *response, size_t response_capacity, size_t *response_len, void *context)` -- CDR bytes both ways -- where rclc's `rclc_service_callback_with_context_t` is `void (*)(const void *request, void *response, void *context)` over DESERIALIZED payloads. The `bool` is not decoration: `srv_raw_try_process` sends a reply only on `ok && resp_len > 0` (`executor/arena.rs`), so returning `false` is how a handler refuses to put a malformed or oversized reply on the wire. rclc's `void` callback cannot refuse at all.

Extension rather than divergence, because the faithful counterpart now SHIPS beside it and carries the correspondence: `packs/c/service.h.jinja` emits `<Srv>_handler_fn_t = void (*)(const <Srv>_request *, <Srv>_response *, void *)` -- rclc's three parameters in rclc's order, with the two payload pointers TYPED -- and the generated trampoline `<Srv>_service_handle_request` is an `nros_service_callback_t` that owns the CDR on both sides. Until W5.e's callers landed (2026-09-18) this byte callback was the only delivery shape and so stood in for rclc's typed one; it is now the byte TIER beside a faithful one, which is where a caller doing its own CDR or FORWARDING a payload belongs.

NOTE WHAT DOES NOT APPEAR HERE: "no allocator". Neither side allocates -- rclc makes the caller own `request_msg` / `response_msg`, and ours puts both structs in the caller's `<Srv>_service_handler_t`.

c:service_get_options.why: reads back the options a service was created with. `nros_service_options_t` ships and `nros_service_init_with_options` takes it; what is missing is the READBACK -- no `*_get_options` exists anywhere in our C surface, for any entity. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417): this row said there is no runtime options struct. Seven ship and the correlator buckets all fourteen items `same` -- `nros_{node,publisher,subscription,service,client,action_client,action_server}_options_t` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/nros_generated.h:1461,1729,2011,2474,2537,2556,2592`) plus a `*_get_default_options` for each, and `nros_node_options_t::domain_id_override` is a RUNTIME per-node domain. What is genuinely absent is the LIFECYCLE around one: no `*_options_copy`, no `*_options_fini`, and no `*_get_options` readback anywhere in the C surface.

c:service_get_rmw_handle.why: our RMW seam is the vtable (RFC-0035), not an entity accessor. See `c:node_get_rmw_handle`.

c:service_impl_t.why: rcl's pimpl; our handles carry their state inline. See `c:publisher_impl_t`.

c:service_init.why:
phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) -- `rcl_service_init(service, node, type_support, service_name, options)`. No symbol answers to this key. The six-argument `nros_service_init` (callback and context in positions 5 and 6) was retired at phase-417 stage 6 step B (`packages/api/nros-c/src/service.rs:303-322`): the callback moved to registration, where rclc puts it (`nros_executor_add_service_raw` <-> `rclc_executor_add_service`). What remains is `rclc_service_init_default` at rclc's arity (`c:service_init_default`, adopt-bounded on the typesupport type) and `nros_service_init_with_qos` / `_with_options` / `_polling` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/nros_generated.h:6194`, `:6246`, `:6293`) for the options-shaped and RFC-0022 polling forms.

ABSENT, not adopt-bounded: see `c:node_init` for why the label is the rcl-layer name's, not the rclc-layer name's.

c:service_init_default.why:
see `c:client_init_default`.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) — refuse-loud -> adopt-bounded. `rclc_service_init_default` EXISTS at rclc's arity (`packages/api/nros-c/src/service.rs:325`: service, node, type, name) and the correlator files it `same`; the old row promised a refusal nothing emits.

WHAT THE COMPILER POINTS AT: argument 3. rclc takes `const rosidl_service_type_support_t*` and a ported file passes `ROSIDL_GET_SRV_TYPE_SUPPORT(pkg, srv, Name)`; ours takes `const struct nros_service_type_t*` (the generated `<name>_type` descriptor, e.g. `&add_two_ints_type` in `examples/threadx-linux/c/service-server/src/main.c:138`). An rcl typesupport pointer at that position is an incompatible-pointer diagnostic on the call, naming both types. That is a mechanical edit, not a message with the migration attached, which is why this is adopt-bounded and not refuse-loud.

THE ENVELOPE: the callback is not on this call in either library — rclc supplies it at `rclc_executor_add_service`, ours at `nros_executor_add_service_raw` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/nros_generated.h:4942`), so that half ports one-for-one. The service-name expansion caveat in `c:publisher_init` does not apply: services reach `resolve_entity_name` at registration.

c:service_init_polling.why: RFC-0022's polling tier. See the pubsub stage's `cpp:PollingSubscription`.

c:service_request_subscription_get_actua.why:
see `c:publisher_get_actual_qos` for the contract and the shape argument.

LANDED phase-444 (issue 1437) — `nros_service_request_subscription_get_actual_qos(const nros_service_t *, nros_qos_t *out)`.

WHY FOUR ACCESSORS AND NOT TWO: one `nros_service_init_with_qos` builds TWO endpoints — a request subscription and a response publisher — and they negotiate against DIFFERENT peers, so the grant is two answers and neither stands for the other. A reliable reply path over a best-effort request path is a working service that drops calls. `rmw_service_t` carries no `qos` field for the same reason, and upstream ships four of these. The pair is computed once per entity kind (`service_granted_qos` / `client_granted_qos`) and each entry point returns one half, so the four cannot disagree about which road a handle is on.

BOTH ROADS ANSWER: L1 (`nros_service_init_polling`) keeps the entity inline in `_opaque`; L2 (`nros_executor_add_service`) hands it to the executor arena and leaves `_internal = (executor_ptr, arena_entry_index)` behind, which `Executor::service_server_handle` resolves. An L2 handle not yet added to an executor answers `NROS_RET_NOT_INIT` — there is no entity to ask, which is a different statement from `UNKNOWN` ("there is an entity and it cannot say").

c:service_response_publisher_get_actual_.why: see `c:service_request_subscription_get_actual_qos` — same call, the other endpoint. LANDED phase-444 (issue 1437).

c:service_send_reply_raw.why: the deprecated `send_reply` spelling of `c:service_send_response_raw`. DEPRECATED ALIAS, phase-379 W5 (2026-08-27). The live spelling is `nros_service_send_response_raw`; this one survived one release as a `NROS_DEPRECATED_MSG` `static inline` forwarder in `nros/service.h`, so an out-of-tree C node that still named it kept compiling and got a diagnostic naming its replacement -- the same shape, and the same reasoning, as `c:param_declare_*`. That was source compatibility only: the forwarder had no external linkage, so `nros_service_send_response_raw` was the sole exported symbol throughout. RETIRED by phase-417 W-B5 (stage 6 step B, commit 4dc5caee9, 2026-09-05), together with `nros_service_send_response` (the pre-polling `NROS_RET_NOT_INIT` stub, forwarded so the un-suffixed name could not read like a second working entry point): `nros/service.h` declares `nros_service_send_response_raw` alone, and the old spelling is an undeclared-identifier error. `service_deprecation_probe.c` was deleted with the forwarder, because an expected-failure compile whose identifier is gone passes while asserting nothing; `packages/api/nros-c/tests/compile/service_reply_entry_point.c` now pins the live signature alone, on the `just check c` lane. Retirement was deferred on purpose until then: the tree's deprecated items retire together on a version boundary, not as parity work (see `rust:BoardConfig::zenoh_locator` in boot.json), and W-B5 was that boundary. Substantive verdict moved to `c:service_send_response_raw`.

rename.residue: NONE since phase-417 W-B5 (stage 6 step B, commit 4dc5caee9, 2026-09-05). The forwarder was retained ON PURPOSE for one release and went in that batch.

c:service_send_response.why: DEPRECATED ALIAS, phase-379 W5 (2026-08-27) -- and the odd member of the pair, because it was never an alias. It was a permanent `NROS_RET_NOT_INIT` stub ("service servers are callback-only through the executor"), left over from before `nros_service_init_polling` and the `_raw` polling pair existed, so no caller can ever have had it succeed. That made it worse than dead once the rename landed: it would have sat on the MORE OBVIOUS name beside the working `nros_service_send_response_raw`, and a consumer migrating off `send_reply` to the name that looks right would have got a runtime NOT_INIT instead of a compile error. So the `#[no_mangle]` export was DELETED and the spelling kept as a `NROS_DEPRECATED_MSG` `static inline` forwarder in `nros/service.h` beside `c:service_send_reply_raw` -- which also makes the call WORK, strictly better than what it did. An object file that referenced the old export must be recompiled; it cannot have been relying on the return value. Its unimplemented twin `nros_service_take_request` was deliberately left alone: which of `take_request` / `try_recv_request_raw` survives is `c:take_request`, still open, and settling half of it here would have pre-empted that row. Substantive verdict moved to `c:service_send_response_raw`.

rename.residue: `nros_service_take_request`, the stub's twin, is still an exported `NROS_RET_NOT_INIT` symbol; it belongs to `c:take_request`.

c:service_send_response_raw.why: the ours-only half of `c:send_response`; recorded so the pair is visible from both sides. LANDED 2026-08-27 (phase-379 W5): this is the renamed `nros_service_send_reply_raw`, and it is now the ONE exported symbol of the reply verb in C. `_raw` is the family convention for the byte-buffer entry points (`nros_publish_raw`, `nros_client_send_request_raw`, the `nros_action_*_raw` family) -- not a marker that a typed non-raw twin exists, because in C there is none. Reached on a server created with `nros_service_init_polling`; `sequence_number` is the value the matching `nros_service_try_recv_request_raw` returned (see `rust:RequestId` for why that token is a bare integer).

c:service_take_request.why: the ours-only half of `c:take_request`. Two entry points carry it: this one, a permanent `NROS_RET_NOT_INIT` stub from before the polling API existed, and `nros_service_take_request_raw`, the L1 polling drain (renamed from `nros_service_try_recv_request_raw` by phase-379 W6 decision 1, 2026-09-03). Which of the two spellings survives is still open.

c:service_take_request_raw.why: the L1 polling-mode drain, the working half of `c:service_take_request`. Byte-oriented for the reason `c:take` names -- no typesupport dispatch, no allocator. Renamed from `nros_service_try_recv_request_raw` by phase-379 W6 decision 1 (2026-09-03).

rust:Service::service_name.why:
see `cpp:Client::get_service_name`.

VERDICT (phase-417 gap-verdict pass, 2026-09-21) — ADOPT-BOUNDED. The reason above holds; what it does not say is WHY this is not the same one-liner as the C++ half, and the difference is the receiver. Our Rust entity handle is a bare arena index with no back-reference — `PublisherHandle { index: usize, _marker }` (`nros-node/src/publisher.rs:10`) — so rclrs's `&self`-only signature cannot reach the string; the name lives in the arena entry, beside the `topic_name` the C `nros_publisher_t` stores. ADOPT-BOUNDED is the honest disposition: take upstream's NAME, on a signature that also takes the node or executor the handle indexes into. The weakening is visible — the compiler demands the argument, which is RFC-0089's mechanical-edit test — and it is forced by the fixed-arena model of RFC-0002, not chosen.

VERDICT (phase-444, 2026-09-21) — DIVERGENCE, for the reason `rust:Publisher::topic_name` states in full, and with the same correction: the ADOPT-BOUNDED premise (an arena index needing the node passed in) was measured and is false. `NodeHandle::create_client` returns `EmbeddedServiceClient`, which owns a `CffiClient` whose `service_name()` has been there all along (`packages/rmw/cffi/src/lib.rs:4581`, `:4712`).

SHIPPED, in one sweep over the whole entity-handle class: `EmbeddedPublisher::topic_name`, `EmbeddedRawPublisher::topic_name`, `Subscription::topic_name`, `RawSubscription::topic_name`, `EmbeddedServiceServer::service_name`, `EmbeddedServiceClient::service_name`, `RawServiceServer::service_name` and `RawServiceClient::service_name` (`packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/handles.rs`). Upstream's verb, upstream's `&self`, no node argument and no arena lookup — each is a one-line forward to the backend handle that has retained the name since it was created.

WHAT IS LEFT IS THE RECEIVER, and `rust:Client` / `rust:Service` already say what it is: rclrs's `Client` is a handle a live node hands back, ours splits into `ServiceClient` (the entity a component DECLARES, RFC-0043/0044) and `ClientTrait` (the RMW seam), with the live handle a third name again, `EmbeddedServiceClient`. No type of ours keys as `Client` or `Service`, so no implementation can close these two rows; what an implementation CAN do, and now has, is make sure the capability is not the thing missing. The C++ halves — `cpp:Client::get_service_name` and `cpp:Service::get_service_name` — did close on this commit and are deleted, because there our class IS `rclcpp::Client`.

NOT ON THE `nros_rmw` TRAIT, which is the one real decision here. `MetadataPublisher` is a ZST and `ZenohPublisher` stores no name, so a required trait method would make every backend keep a SECOND 256-byte copy of a string the C-ABI shim above it already holds, on targets that count bytes. `actual_qos` (issue 1437) IS on the trait because only a backend can answer it; a name is handed IN at create and retained one layer up.
